name: Jeroham
overview: Jeroham was a male Levite known uniquely as the son of Pashhur, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 9:12. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation with Levi, which is significant in the biblical context for priestly and temple duties. There are no additional notes or details about his life beyond this familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroham means 'he will be compassionate.' This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 9:12, does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects a meaningful Hebrew name that may indicate a character trait or hoped-for attribute.
familyAndRelationships: Jeroham is explicitly identified as the son of Pashhur and is inferred to be the father of Adaiah, according to 1 Chronicles 9:12. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroham's mention in 1 Chronicles 9:12 situates him within the genealogical records of the Levites, emphasizing his role in the priestly lineage. His connection as the son of Pashhur links him to a family involved in temple service or religious duties. Although the biblical text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his inclusion highlights the importance of preserving the heritage of those serving in God's house.
